claims.statement: Polish law requires healthcare entities using medical devices to retain documentation of installation, repair, maintenance, service, software updates, inspections, adjustment, calibration, and safety checks, including next-due dates, for at least five years after use ends.
The EU Medical Device Regulation requires instructions for use, where relevant, to state the nature and frequency of preventive and regular maintenance and necessary calibration.
Small clinics likely experience a coordination and evidence problem across mixed-brand service providers, but no authoritative source found quantifies its frequency or current spend.

contrary_evidence: Many devices are already covered by OEM service contracts, distributors, spreadsheets, or clinic-management systems.
Incorrect schedules or provider qualification checks create patient-safety and liability exposure.
Small clinics may have too few devices or too little enforcement pressure to justify a recurring subscription.

economics.acquisition_route: Embed enrollment at equipment lease or insurance inception and renewal, when serials and asset values are already captured; each financed device receives a record and next-due workflow by default. For direct acquisition, offer a paid gap report based on a one-hour barcode inventory rather than generic outbound consulting.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A normalized manufacturer-instruction and service-interval library, verified qualification rules, regional service capacity, standardized completion evidence, and aggregated purchasing reduce missed dates and quote friction. Trusted audit trails plus service fulfillment create value beyond reminders.
fingerprint.customer: Polish private clinics, dental and physiotherapy chains, and diagnostic centers with 50-500 mixed-brand medical devices but no biomedical-engineering department.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed enrollment at equipment lease or insurance inception and renewal, when serials and asset values are already captured; each financed device receives a record and next-due workflow by default. For direct acquisition, offer a paid gap report based on a one-hour barcode inventory rather than generic outbound consulting.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Scan device identifiers and manufacturer instructions, build the required maintenance and calibration calendar, issue reminders, verify provider qualifications and completed work fields, compare service quotes, and retain audit-ready records for the required period. The venture coordinates evidence and procurement; qualified technicians perform all maintenance and safety checks.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The clinic pays a site-onboarding and asset-normalization fee, then an annual per-device subscription for schedule control and documentation; it pays a fixed coordination fee when the desk tenders and closes a service or calibration event.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A scheduled review, calibration, software update, acquisition, insurer or accreditation request, missing technical passport, or device failure exposes fragmented service records and unclear next-due dates.

founder_fit: Strong fit with health interest, structured data, automation, document extraction, and a nearby medical perspective for customer-language discovery.
Can start with low capital and asynchronous evidence work while all technical service remains outsourced.
The medical relationship is not distribution or authorization; the founder needs formal clinical, legal, and biomedical-engineering review.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: Medical-Device Maintenance Evidence Control Tower
uncertainties: Average device count, overdue-document rate, and annual service spend in the target clinic segment.
Whether lessors and insurers can lawfully and technically embed the workflow at origination.
Scope of professional liability and the acceptable boundary between record coordination and technical judgment.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Run paid 30-day inventories at ten unrelated private clinics totaling at least 500 devices, have a biomedical engineer review the generated schedules, and measure missing records, overdue events, and quote variance. Continue only if at least two clinics sign annual contracts and the review finds no unsafe scheduling errors.
